title: Accident & Near-Miss Reporting
blurb: Why every accident and near-miss gets reported, what to do first, and why there is no blame.
siteNotes: Where the accident book is kept and how to complete it (your manager will show you).
Who the Duty Manager is on each shift.
Where the first aid kit and first aiders are.
legalNotes: Employers must record workplace accidents, and report certain injuries, diseases and dangerous occurrences to HSE under RIDDOR: Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations 2013. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1471

CHECK: the trainer says to write up the accident book "before the end of your shift". That is the venue's own rule rather than a legal deadline; please confirm it is what you want. RIDDOR reporting (to HSE) is the manager's job and is not taught in this trainer.
CHECK: "behind most serious accidents there were usually lots of near-misses" echoes the well-known safety pyramid, which is a rule of thumb rather than a proven law; the slide softens it to "often".
See also the first-aid and accidents session in the library.

cards.title: Accident & Near-Miss Reporting
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say what a near-miss is and why it matters
- know what to do first and who to tell
- explain why there is no blame for reporting

cards.title: Free warnings
cards.body:
If someone slips on a wet floor but catches themselves and is not hurt, is it worth mentioning? Absolutely yes.

That is a near-miss: an event that could have caused harm but did not, this time. Near-misses are basically free warnings.

items.title: The box
items.text: That nearly fell off a shelf.

cards.title: Report the small stuff, prevent the big stuff
cards.body: Behind most serious accidents there were usually lots of near-misses first. If we hear about the near-miss, we can fix the cause before anyone actually gets hurt.

items.title: Near-misses
items.text: Report these and we can stop everything above.

items.title: Minor accidents
items.text: Small injuries that get shrugged off.

cards.title: Report ALL of them
cards.body:
Report all accidents and near-misses, however minor they seem. If someone is hurt, deal with that first: make the area safe and get first aid.

Then tell the Duty Manager and make sure it is written up in the accident book before the end of your shift, while it is still fresh in everyone's mind.

items.title: Help the person
items.text: Make the area safe and get first aid.

cards.title: Reporting is never about blame
cards.body:
There is NO blame for reporting. We are not looking for someone to point the finger at. We are looking to learn and improve so it does not happen again.

If it is a serious emergency, call 999 straight away.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Report ALL accidents and near-misses, however minor
- If someone is hurt, deal with that first
- Tell the Duty Manager and write it in the accident book before the end of your shift
- There is no blame for reporting
- In a serious emergency, call 999 straight away
